Archive Before Estate

The best moment to begin an archive is while the founder can still explain why a decision was made, what failed, who carried it, and what should never be repeated.

Read the exhibition

00

The proposition

Estate planning asks what should happen after incapacity or death. A living archive begins earlier and answers a different operational question: what knowledge must be captured before silence makes the record ambiguous?

National Archives guidance emphasizes requirements for managing electronic records. Smithsonian preservation resources distinguish collections care, storage, handling, and textile-conservation needs. These sources do not supply a bespoke succession plan; they establish practical preservation disciplines that a fashion practice can adapt with professional advice.

01–04

The institutional sequence

DAY 01 · INVENTORY

Name what exists.

Create identifiers for garments, samples, sketches, patterns, specifications, correspondence, photographs, recordings, contracts, accounts, and born-digital files.

VERIFIEDS08S39

DAY 02 · PAIR

Reconnect object and file.

Pair physical location with filenames, versions, photographs, condition notes, creator credits, and related agreements so neither half becomes orphaned.

PROPOSALS39S40

DAY 03 · NARRATE

Capture the decision voice.

Record short founder and collaborator accounts: the problem, alternatives, refusal, compromise, failure, and what changed afterward. Preserve transcripts with the recording.

INFERENCES08S39

DAY 04–07 · STEWARD

Protect access and future meaning.

Document formats, backups, storage conditions, privacy, rights, account recovery, successor access, conservation referrals, and a schedule for reviewing the archive.

VERIFIEDS40S41S42S43

COUNTERPOINT

What this framework could get wrong

Preservation is selective power. A founder-centered archive can erase the patternmaker, sewer, model, photographer, assistant, client, and community knowledge that carried the institution. The archive plan must ask who is missing and who may describe the work.

FIELDWORK

Do the work now

Use this as a working session, not a score.

  1. Choose one garment and assign a persistent internal identifier.
  2. Pair it with every related physical and digital record.
  3. Record a five-minute account from the founder and one collaborator.
  4. Document rights, privacy, storage, backup, access, and professional-referral needs.
